newsitem.title: USA: U.S. trade gap rises 17.0 percent in May.
newsitem.headline: U.S. trade gap rises 17.0 percent in May.

text.p: The U.S. trade deficit in May soared by 17.0 percent to $10.23 billion as imports rose for the seventh straight month to a record high, the Commerce Department said on Friday.

The department said May exports fell 0.8 percent to $77.2 billion, reflecting a drop in exports of capital goods, such as telecommunications equipment. Imports continued their steady upward march, rising by a modest 1.0 percent in May to $87.5 billion, led by demand for capital goods, primarily civilian aircraft and automobiles, the department said.
